stages.title: See what Pack the Rucksack does and how a round plays

screens.title: Look at a round of Pack the Rucksack, from the first item to the score

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how a round of Pack the Rucksack plays and how it scores.
Pack the Rucksack is a sorting game. It is on Slieve Binnian, the first place on the Summit Ready map.
You choose any 4 of the 8 game chapters to build. You may build more than 4 if you have time.
First you build Pack the Rucksack exactly as it is in Summit Ready. Then, in stage 5, you change it into a sorting game on your own topic.
A round starts with 12 [[kit cards|1]] on the kit pile along the top. Each card shows a picture of one item, with its name under the picture.
6 of the items belong in a rucksack for a day on the hills, and 6 should stay at home. The 12 come at random from 25 items, so every round is different.
You [[drag and drop|3]] each card into one of two [[zones|2]]: **Pack it** or **Leave it at home**. Until you check, you can move any card again, to anywhere.
When the pile is empty, you press **Check my rucksack**. Each card in the right zone turns light green, with a tick. Each card in the wrong zone turns light red, with a cross.

The score is the number of cards in the right zone, times 100, divided by 12 and rounded down. So 12 right scores 100 points, 11 right scores 91 points and 10 right scores 83 points.

words: MouseEventArgs
The kind of information that `e` holds when a mouse event runs. It says where the mouse was and which button was pressed.
kit card
One of the 12 items you sort in Pack the Rucksack. In the code, each kit card is a button.
zone
A place where you drop a kit card: the kit pile, Pack it, or Leave it at home.
drag and drop
Pressing the mouse button on something, moving the mouse while you hold the button, and letting go over the place it should go.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Name` on a KitItem. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `KitItem.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<KitItem>` is a list that holds KitItem objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
bool
A value that is either true or false. `Pack` is a bool: true to pack the item, false to leave it.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `cards[0]` is the first kit card, and `cards[11]` is the 12th.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the 3 zones.
FlowLayoutPanel
A panel that lines up the controls on it by itself, left to right, then onto the next row. Each zone is a FlowLayoutPanel.
foreach
`foreach` runs a loop once for each thing in a list or an array, such as each card in `cards`.
Tag
A spare property that every control has. It can hold any object you like. Each kit card keeps its KitItem in its Tag.
AllowDrop
A property that lets a control take a drop. Only a control with AllowDrop true can have a kit card dropped on it.
MouseDown
The event that happens the moment the mouse button is pressed on a control, before it is let go.
DoDragDrop
Starts a drag. The thing being dragged goes with the mouse until the button is let go.
DragEnter
The event that happens when something being dragged moves onto a control.
DragDrop
The event that happens when something being dragged is let go over a control.
typeof
`typeof(Button)` names the type Button, so that code can ask for the Button being dragged.
Parent
The control that another control sits on. A kit card in the Pack it zone has flpPack as its Parent.
is
`is` asks whether a value is of a type. `target is Button` is true when the target is a button.
Bitmap
A picture held in memory. `new Bitmap(picture, 64, 64)` makes a copy of a picture 64 pixels wide and 64 pixels tall.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(227, 241, 228)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
whole-number division
`/` between two whole numbers drops anything after the decimal point. `1100 / 12` is 91, not 91.67.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a drop on a zone.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Card_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Card_Click`.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Card_Click` is the handler for a click on any kit card.
Controls.Add
Puts a control onto a window or a panel. If the control is already on another panel, it moves off that panel.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the card that was clicked.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Button)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a button.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
ToLower
Gives a copy of some text in small letters. `"Map".ToLower()` gives `"map"`.
red underline
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.

box.title: If a file is missing or broken

blocks.p: Pack the Rucksack checks its data file before it deals any cards. This is what you see instead of a crash.

If `kit.txt` is missing, or has fewer than 6 good `pack` lines or 6 good `leave` lines, no cards appear. The line along the bottom says **Pack the Rucksack needs 6 items to pack and 6 to leave in Data\kit.txt.**
If a line of `kit.txt` does not have exactly 4 parts, Pack the Rucksack skips that line.
If `icon-rucksack-64.png` is missing, the Pack it zone has no rucksack picture.
If a sound is missing, that moment is silent, and the game carries on.
Every kit picture must be there, because each card makes a small copy of its picture. If one is missing, the game stops with an error when the window opens.
To put a missing file back, you download the [[zip file|5]] again and paste its folders into bin\Debug. When Windows asks about the files you already have, you click **Skip these files**.
Skipping keeps every file you already have, including any file you changed. Only the missing files are copied in.

code.title: KitItem.cs: the KitItem class
code.why: You type the 4 properties, and the 4 lines that put a value into each one, because they are new. The rest reads a file the same way as `LoadAll` in chapter 3, so it comes in the copy.
partLines: The class and its 4 properties

`class KitItem` starts the class. Each property holds one part of a line of `kit.txt`. `Picture` holds the picture's file name, and `Name` holds the item's name. `Pack` is a bool: true if the item goes in the rucksack, false if it stays at home. `Reason` holds why. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read each property and change it.
The constructor

This part is the constructor. It runs when code writes `new KitItem(parts)`. `parts` is one line of `kit.txt`, already cut into 4 pieces at each bar. `parts[2] == "pack"` is true when the third part says `pack`, so `Pack` becomes true. For `leave`, `Pack` becomes false.
The start of LoadAll

`static` means that you call LoadAll on the class itself, as `KitItem.LoadAll()`. You do not need a KitItem object first. LoadAll starts with an empty list. `Files.Data` from chapter 2 gives the full path of `kit.txt` in the Data folder. If `kit.txt` is not there, LoadAll hands back the empty list, so the game shows a message and does not crash.
Read every line

The StreamReader is the tool that reads a file. It opens `kit.txt`. The loop goes round once for each line, until the end of the file. `Split('|')` cuts each line at each bar into `parts`. If a line does not have exactly 4 parts, `continue` skips it and the loop moves on to the next line. Every good line becomes a new KitItem, and `items.Add` puts it on the end of the list.
Close the file and hand back the list
`reader.Close()` closes `kit.txt`, so that other programs can open it again. `return items;` hands the full list back to the code that called LoadAll.

screens.title: Fill in frmRucksack_Load, which reads the kit when the window opens

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, frmRucksack reads the kit and sorts it into items to pack and items to leave, as the window opens.
frmRucksack_Load is the empty method you made in stage 3. It runs once, right before the window first appears. You type the yellow lines inside it now. Later in this stage you add 5 more lines to it.

code.title: frmRucksack_Load
partLines: The speaker and the rucksack
ShowSpeaker, from chapter 9, puts the right speaker picture on the header strip. `Files.Picture` from chapter 2 loads the rucksack picture from Images\Icons into picPackIcon.
Two empty lists
`pack` will hold every item that goes in the rucksack. `leave` will hold every item that stays at home.
Sort the kit into the two lists

`KitItem.LoadAll()` reads `kit.txt` and gives back a list, with one KitItem for each line. `foreach` goes through that list one item at a time. An item whose `Pack` is true goes into `pack`. Every other item goes into `leave`.
Not enough items

A round needs 6 items of each kind. With fewer, the line along the bottom shows a message. Then `return` stops frmRucksack_Load early, so no cards appear. Inside quotes, `\\` stands for one backslash, so the message shows Data\kit.txt.
Deal the cards
`DealCards` picks the 12 items and deals them onto the kit pile. You write it on the next screen.

code.title: DealCards
partLines: Two shuffled orders
`chosen` has room for the 12 items of this round. `packOrder` holds the numbers of the items in `pack`, in a random order. `leaveOrder` does the same for `leave`.
Pick 6 of each
The loop runs 6 times. Each time, it takes the next item from the shuffled `pack` list into places 0 to 5. It takes the next item from the shuffled `leave` list into places 6 to 11.
Mix and deal all 12

partLines: A heading
ZoneOf gives back a FlowLayoutPanel: the zone. `is` asks whether the target's Tag holds a FlowLayoutPanel. Each heading keeps its zone in its Tag, so a drop on a heading goes to that zone.

stages.title: Change Pack the Rucksack into a game on your own topic

screens.title: Choose your own items, and 2 more things to change

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you have chosen your own items to sort, and 2 more things to change.
Your own game keeps the Pack the Rucksack code, but uses your own topic. Each item has a picture, a name, which of the 2 zones it belongs in, and a reason. Any topic with 2 groups like that works.
Recycling: a picture of some rubbish, its name, recycle or not, and why.
Healthy eating: a picture of a food, its name, every day or now and then, and why.
Online safety: a picture of something you might share, its name, safe to share or keep private, and why.
You need at least 6 items for each zone, so that every round has 6 of each. More is better, because then the rounds differ more.

Change at least 2 more things as well, so that your game plays differently from Pack the Rucksack. For example, change the pass mark for the happy sound, the colours, the size of the cards or the feedback lines.
Every picture and sound you use must be free to use. Add a line for each one to `credits.txt`, so its maker gets the credit. Say who made it, its licence (the rules for using it) and a link.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, your game reads your own data file and shows your own pictures.
Your own files go in the same folders as the Summit Ready files, inside bin\Debug. Your data file goes in Data, your pictures go in a folder inside Images, and any new sounds go in Sounds.

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you have chosen how many points your game gives, and every total fits.
You choose how many points each item sorted into the right zone is worth. Summit Ready gives 100 points for all 12 items right.
Your top score is what a perfect round earns. For example, 12 items at 5 points each gives a top score of 60.

glossary: MouseEventArgs
The kind of information that `e` holds when a mouse event runs. It says where the mouse was and which button was pressed.
kit card
One of the 12 items you sort in Pack the Rucksack. In the code, each kit card is a button.
zone
A place where you drop a kit card: the kit pile, Pack it, or Leave it at home.
drag and drop
Pressing the mouse button on something, moving the mouse while you hold the button, and letting go over the place it should go.
bin\Debug
The folder inside your project where Visual Studio 2019 puts the program it builds. Summit Ready reads its data, pictures and sounds from there.
zip file
One file with other files and folders packed inside it.
property
A named value that an object carries, such as `Name` on a KitItem. `{ get; set; }` lets other code read the value and change it.
constructor
A method with the same name as its class. It runs once, when code makes a new object with `new`.
static
A method marked `static` belongs to the class itself. You call it on the class name, as in `KitItem.LoadAll()`.
List
A list that grows as you add to it. `List<KitItem>` is a list that holds KitItem objects.
continue
Inside a loop, `continue` skips the rest of this turn of the loop. The loop goes straight on to its next turn.
bool
A value that is either true or false. `Pack` is a bool: true to pack the item, false to leave it.
lightning bolt
The button at the top of the Properties window that shows a control's events in place of its properties.
field
A variable written at the top of the class, outside every method. Every method in the form can use it, and it keeps its value until the window closes.
array
A row of values of the same type, kept together under one name and numbered from 0. `cards[0]` is the first kit card, and `cards[11]` is the 12th.
panel
A control that holds other controls. `pnlPlay` is the play area that holds the 3 zones.
FlowLayoutPanel
A panel that lines up the controls on it by itself, left to right, then onto the next row. Each zone is a FlowLayoutPanel.
foreach
`foreach` runs a loop once for each thing in a list or an array, such as each card in `cards`.
Tag
A spare property that every control has. It can hold any object you like. Each kit card keeps its KitItem in its Tag.
AllowDrop
A property that lets a control take a drop. Only a control with AllowDrop true can have a kit card dropped on it.
MouseDown
The event that happens the moment the mouse button is pressed on a control, before it is let go.
DoDragDrop
Starts a drag. The thing being dragged goes with the mouse until the button is let go.
DragEnter
The event that happens when something being dragged moves onto a control.
DragDrop
The event that happens when something being dragged is let go over a control.
typeof
`typeof(Button)` names the type Button, so that code can ask for the Button being dragged.
Parent
The control that another control sits on. A kit card in the Pack it zone has flpPack as its Parent.
is
`is` asks whether a value is of a type. `target is Button` is true when the target is a button.
Bitmap
A picture held in memory. `new Bitmap(picture, 64, 64)` makes a copy of a picture 64 pixels wide and 64 pixels tall.
colour from red, green and blue
`Color.FromArgb(227, 241, 228)` mixes a colour from red, green and blue. Each number is from 0 to 255.
whole-number division
`/` between two whole numbers drops anything after the decimal point. `1100 / 12` is 91, not 91.67.
event
Something that happens to a control, such as a click on a button, or a drop on a zone.
connect with +=
`+=` connects a method to an event in code. `card.Click += Card_Click;` means that a click on that card runs `Card_Click`.
handler
The method that runs when an event happens. `Card_Click` is the handler for a click on any kit card.
Controls.Add
Puts a control onto a window or a panel. If the control is already on another panel, it moves off that panel.
sender
Every handler is given `sender`: the control that the event happened to, such as the card that was clicked.
cast
A type in brackets in front of a value tells C# what the value really is. `(Button)sender` tells C# that `sender` is a button.
or
`||` means or. The `if` is true when any one of its parts is true.
ToLower
Gives a copy of some text in small letters. `"Map".ToLower()` gives `"map"`.
red underline
The wavy red line Visual Studio 2019 draws under code it does not understand yet. Often it means a method you have not written yet.
